mascotLines: Recurring invoices stopped marking themselves ‘Completed’ after just one payment. I only declare nap time complete once all four legs stop twitching.
Inbox+ is cutting down on repeat notifications. I will, however, still bark at the mailman every single day. Some traditions are non-negotiable.
You can now sort pipeline jobs by Intake Date. I sort my toys by ‘most recently stolen from the couch’ — it's a simpler system, but it works for me.
Clients can finally pay $0 invoices from the mobile app. I have never once complained about being paid zero treats for a trick. Growth mindset.

items.text: Sort pipeline jobs by more fields, including Intake Date
items.desc: Sorting inside the pipeline view used to be limited and unreliable — fields like Intake Date and Internal Deadline were only sortable from the Jobs page. Now pipeline sorting includes those same fields and behaves consistently, so you don't have to jump back to the Jobs page just to sort your work the way you want.

Both the “Assigned to me” and “All Accounts” email pages now have a filter for read/unread status, so you can quickly pull up just the threads that still need a reply instead of scanning the whole list.

Inbox+ (the notifications hub) is getting decluttered in beta — fewer low-value or duplicate notifications, related notifications grouped together, and more consistent-looking cards with quick actions like reply or assign built right in. Limited rollout.

items.text: Recurring invoices marked themselves “Completed” after just one payment
items.desc: If a client signed a proposal with a recurring, autopay invoice, the invoice's status could flip from Active to Completed right after the very first scheduled payment — even if that payment failed, and even with many payments still left on the schedule. Fixed so the status now reflects what's actually happened.

items.text: Billing cycle upgrades could skip the invoice entirely
items.desc: Upgrading a firm to a longer billing cycle (say, 1 year to 2 years) while it had a lot of bonus time banked could extend the subscription for free, with no invoice ever created in Stripe. Fixed so these upgrades are billed correctly.

items.text: “Pending Signature” filter could error out on large firms
items.desc: Filtering the Clients page by “Pending Signature,” or just viewing pending-signature counts, could throw a server error on firms with a lot of signature requests. Fixed with a faster, more reliable query.

items.text: A specific organizer checklist item could vanish from view
items.desc: Adding the “Health Insurance (1095)” item to an organizer's Document Checklist through Edit Checklist could make that item invisible in both the firm and client view, while the item count also went out of sync (showing “0 of 6” with only 5 items listed). Fixed.

items.text: Clients couldn't pay $0 invoices from the mobile app
items.desc: Clients could already pay a $0 invoice on the web portal, but trying to do the same from the mobile app threw a “Value must be greater than 0” error instead. Fixed so $0 invoices can be paid on mobile too.

items.text: Paying small invoices in the mobile app showed a generic “Error”
items.desc: Trying to pay an invoice under $0.50 in the mobile app just showed a bare “Error” message with no explanation. It now shows the same clear message clients already see on the web.

items.text: Recurring invoice descriptions were missing in the mobile app
items.desc: The Description field filled in while setting up a recurring invoice inside a proposal wasn't showing up when the client viewed that proposal in the mobile app. Fixed so it displays there like it does everywhere else.

mystery: Nothing hidden in the vault this week — every single thing we shipped is already sitting up there in plain sight. Even I couldn't find anything to bury.
